scenario: Gamma 后端面试，被问 GMV Max 项目里的一个取舍。她当场卡成「keeping the implementation simple and make the simple and make the system flexible」，把 simple/flexible 绕成一团、丢了线。
scenario_en: In the Gamma backend interview she's asked about a tradeoff in the GMV Max project. She jams on "keeping the implementation simple and make the simple and make the system flexible" and loses the thread.
q: 这个「简单 vs 灵活」的取舍，怎么一句说清并拍板？
q_en: How do you state this "simple vs flexible" tradeoff in one line and commit?
options: The tradeoff was, keeping the implementation simple and make the simple and, make the system flexible enough for future promotion models, so, let me think how to say this...
The tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility. I leaned toward the simpler design, since we only had two promotion models — I'd revisit it when a third one shows up.
I built the system to be as flexible as possible, so it could support any promotion model we might add later.
There were certain tradeoffs between simplicity and flexibility that I had to take into consideration in the design.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：一句「X versus Y」+ 拍板 vs 把 simple/flexible 绕成一团、never lands。
why: 把取舍压成一句「simplicity versus flexibility」，再用「I leaned toward… because…」拍板并给触发条件。她的毛病是绕着 simple/flexible 打转、never lands。
why_en: Name the axis in one line — simplicity versus flexibility — then commit with "I leaned toward the simpler one because..." instead of looping on the words.
whenOtherWins: 如果两边都还没数据支撑、面试官只想听你识别出取舍存在，那点出 axis、暂不拍板也可以接受。
options_en: The tradeoff was, keeping the implementation simple and make the simple and, make the system flexible enough for future promotion models, so, let me think how to say this...
The tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility. I leaned toward the simpler design, since we only had two promotion models — I'd revisit it when a third one shows up.
I built the system to be as flexible as possible, so it could support any promotion model we might add later.
There were certain tradeoffs between simplicity and flexibility that I had to take into consideration in the design.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：把两个词绕成一团、说不到底。
选项主张：一句点名取舍轴，再拍板给条件。
选项主张：只说做得尽量灵活，不提代价。
选项主张：泛泛说「有一些取舍要考虑」。
optionScenarioImpacts: 绕圈丢线，面试官只看到你说不清取舍。
点名加拍板，显示你想清楚了也能讲出来。
只讲好处不讲代价，像没真正权衡过。
空话一句，等于没回答这个取舍。
optionMeanings_en: Loop on simple and flexible without landing.
One line X versus Y, then commit with I leaned toward.
Just say you made it as flexible as possible.
Vaguely say there were tradeoffs to consider.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Looping loses the thread; they see you can't state a tradeoff.
Naming plus committing shows you thought it through.
Upside only reads as never having weighed the cost.
Vague talk answers nothing about the actual tradeoff.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: loop without landing.
Use when you must state the axis and pick a side out loud.
Only fits when this statement is true: flexibility only.
Only fits when this statement is true: vague tradeoff talk.

scenario: IKEA/ML 面试讲后端 workflow refactor 的取舍。她说成「one trade off is that this refactor takes some time, but the first trade off was the speed of migration versus the production safety」，绕了两圈才点到。
scenario_en: In the IKEA/ML interview she describes a tradeoff in a backend workflow refactor: "one tradeoff is that this refactor takes some time, but the first tradeoff was the speed of migration versus the production safety" — two loops before she lands it.
q: 「迁移速度 vs 生产安全」，怎么用「buys us… but costs us…」说清？
q_en: How do you frame "migration speed vs production safety" with "buys us... but costs us..."?
options: One tradeoff is that this refactor takes some time, but the first tradeoff was, the speed of migration versus the production safety, so, technically we had to rewrite more aggressively...
We rewrote the workflow aggressively so the migration would go as fast as possible and we could ship the refactor sooner.
There was a tradeoff around migration speed and production safety that we needed to be careful about here.
A faster migration buys us an earlier ship date but costs us production safety. On a mature system I chose the slower, safer rollout.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：一句「buys us X but costs us Y」+ 拍板 vs 「the first trade off was… takes some time」绕两圈。
why: 用「A buys us X but costs us Y」把收益和代价一句话摆平，再拍板选安全。她的问题是绕「the first trade off / takes time」，代价说不利落。
why_en: Say "a faster migration buys us an earlier ship but costs us safety," then commit — don't loop on "the first tradeoff was... takes some time."
whenOtherWins: 如果这是一个抛弃型原型、坏了也没影响，那直接选「快」而少谈安全代价也说得过去。
options_en: One tradeoff is that this refactor takes some time, but the first tradeoff was, the speed of migration versus the production safety, so, technically we had to rewrite more aggressively...
We rewrote the workflow aggressively so the migration would go as fast as possible and we could ship the refactor sooner.
There was a tradeoff around migration speed and production safety that we needed to be careful about here.
A faster migration buys us an earlier ship date but costs us production safety. On a mature system I chose the slower, safer rollout.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：在原因前绕两圈才点到取舍。
选项主张：只说要快、要早点上线，不提代价。
选项主张：泛泛说有个速度与安全的取舍。
选项主张：一句摆平收益与代价后选安全。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两圈才点到，面试官觉得你没理清。
只求快，暴露你没在意生产风险。
点了名却不拍板，收不了尾。
收益代价一句清，还给出决定。
optionMeanings_en: Loop on "takes some time / the first tradeoff."
Only say go fast and ship sooner, no cost.
Vaguely note a speed-vs-safety tradeoff.
Buys us X but costs us Y, then commit to safe.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two loops before landing reads as unclear thinking.
Speed only signals you ignored production risk.
Names it but never commits, so it trails off.
One line of gain and cost, plus a decision.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: loop before landing.
Only fits when this statement is true: speed only.
Only fits when this statement is true: no commitment.
Use when you must weigh gain vs cost then commit.

scenario: Alterion 技术面问数据库怎么分。她说「I would separate the read pass and the write pass... because it's half acid」——把 read path 说成「read pass」，把 ACID 说成「half acid」。
scenario_en: In the Alterion technical interview she's asked how to split the database. She says "I would separate the read pass and the write pass... because it's half acid" — "read pass" for read path, "half acid" for ACID.
q: 「强一致 → 选 SQL」这个取舍，怎么一句说清并拍板？
q_en: How do you state the "strong consistency → SQL" tradeoff in one line and commit?
options: The tradeoff is strong consistency versus write scale. These campaign writes must stay consistent, so I'd lean toward a SQL store like Postgres.
So I would separate the read pass and the write pass, and use SQL like MySQL, because it's half acid, so the data can be, more consistent I think.
I'd just use Postgres, since SQL databases are ACID and give you strong consistency out of the box.
There's a consistency tradeoff here, so I'd pick whichever database keeps our data most consistent.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「consistency versus write scale」+ 拍板 vs 「read pass / half acid」错词形。
why: 先点名「strong consistency versus write scale」，再因为写必须一致而拍板选 SQL。她的错词形是「read pass」（应为 read path）、「half acid」（应为 ACID）。
why_en: Name it — strong consistency versus write scale — then commit to SQL because writes must stay consistent; it's read path, not "read pass," and ACID, not "half acid."
whenOtherWins: 如果写入量极大、又能接受最终一致，那该反过来选可水平扩展的 NoSQL，牺牲强一致换写扩展。
options_en: The tradeoff is strong consistency versus write scale. These campaign writes must stay consistent, so I'd lean toward a SQL store like Postgres.
So I would separate the read pass and the write pass, and use SQL like MySQL, because it's half acid, so the data can be, more consistent I think.
I'd just use Postgres, since SQL databases are ACID and give you strong consistency out of the box.
There's a consistency tradeoff here, so I'd pick whichever database keeps our data most consistent.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：点名一致性与写扩展后选 SQL。
选项主张：说成 read pass / half acid 的错词形。
选项主张：只夸 SQL 一致，不提写扩展代价。
选项主张：泛泛说选更一致的那个库。
optionScenarioImpacts: 点名加拍板，理由扣住写必须一致。
错词形一出，面试官怀疑你真懂不懂。
只讲优点，漏掉牺牲的写扩展。
没点名取舍轴，也没真的选出来。
optionMeanings_en: Consistency versus write scale, then commit to SQL.
Wrong forms: "read pass" and "half acid."
Praise SQL consistency, skip the scale cost.
Vaguely pick the more consistent database.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Names it and commits, tied to writes staying consistent.
Wrong word forms make them doubt you understand.
Upside only, drops the write-scale sacrifice.
No axis named and no real choice made.
optionDirectness_en: Use when writes must stay consistent and you commit.
Only fits when this statement is true: wrong word forms.
Only fits when this statement is true: SQL upside only.
Only fits when this statement is true: no axis named.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库的四个事务保证；说全称，别说成「half acid」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the set of transaction guarantees a relational database gives — say the letters, not "half acid."

termDefinitions.meaning: 读请求走的那条链路；口语是 read path，不是 read pass。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The read path is the route a read request takes through the system — it's read path, not "read pass."

scenario: Alterion 面试问哪些服务该走异步。她说「for the service that is not time sensitive, that I would decouple with some queue to debug, decouple, and don't interrupt or mean flow」——卡在 decouple 上重复。
scenario_en: In the Alterion interview she's asked which services should go async. She says "for the service that is not time sensitive, I would decouple with some queue to, decouple, and don't interrupt or mean flow" — stuck repeating decouple.
q: 「非实时工作放队列」，怎么用「buys us… but costs us…」说清？
q_en: How do you frame "put non-urgent work on a queue" with "buys us... but costs us..."?
options: For the service that is not time sensitive, I would decouple with some queue to, decouple, so it don't interrupt the main flow, decouple it...
I'd push the non-urgent work onto a message queue so it never blocks the main request flow at all.
Putting the non-urgent work on a queue buys us a non-blocking main flow but costs us immediacy — the result is only eventually consistent.
For things that aren't time sensitive I'd handle them separately somehow so they don't slow down the main flow.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「buys us X but costs us Y」+ 拍板 vs 卡在 decouple 上重复三遍。
why: 「Putting it on a queue buys us a non-blocking flow but costs us immediacy」——一句摆平收益和代价。她的问题是 decouple 空转、说不出付出了什么。
why_en: Say "a queue buys us a non-blocking main flow but costs us immediacy," instead of spinning on the word decouple.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个工作必须同步拿到结果才能继续（比如支付授权），那就别上队列，宁可阻塞也要即时。
options_en: For the service that is not time sensitive, I would decouple with some queue to, decouple, so it don't interrupt the main flow, decouple it...
I'd push the non-urgent work onto a message queue so it never blocks the main request flow at all.
Putting the non-urgent work on a queue buys us a non-blocking main flow but costs us immediacy — the result is only eventually consistent.
For things that aren't time sensitive I'd handle them separately somehow so they don't slow down the main flow.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：卡在同一个词上重复三遍。
选项主张：只说队列不阻塞，不提即时性代价。
选项主张：收益代价一句清，代价落到最终一致。
选项主张：泛泛说单独处理、别拖慢主流程。
optionScenarioImpacts: 空转重复，面试官听不出你要说什么。
只讲好处，漏了结果不再即时的代价。
一句摆平得失，代价说到最终一致。
没点名队列，也没说付出了什么。
optionMeanings_en: Spin on the word decouple three times.
Queue is non-blocking, but no cost stated.
Buys us X but costs us Y, plus eventual consistency.
Vaguely handle it separately, no cost named.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Spinning repetition leaves them unsure of your point.
Upside only drops the loss of immediacy.
Gain and cost in one line, cost is eventual consistency.
No queue named and no cost stated.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: spin on decouple.
Only fits when this statement is true: non-blocking only.
Use when you weigh non-blocking against immediacy.
Only fits when this statement is true: vague handling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写完后各处不是立刻一致，过一会儿才收敛到同一状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventually consistent means the data isn't in sync the instant you write it, but converges to the same state a moment later.

scenario: IKEA/ML 面试问她何时选 XGBoost 而不是深度学习。她答得对，但把「什么条件下会反转」说成一长串「when the problem is mainly based on some structure feature, when the data set is not extremely large」，没利落收口。
scenario_en: In the IKEA/ML interview she's asked when she'd pick XGBoost over deep learning. Her reasons are right but she trails through "when the problem is mainly based on some structure feature, when the data set is not extremely large" without landing.
q: 怎么用「I'd lean toward X, but if Z changes I'd switch to Y」把这个选择说清？
q_en: How do you frame this with "I'd lean toward X, but if Z changes I'd switch to Y"?
options: It depends on the data really — sometimes XGBoost is better and sometimes deep learning is better, it's kind of case by case.
For structured, smaller data I'd lean toward XGBoost for speed. But if the data gets huge or unstructured, I'd switch to deep learning.
I'd just go with XGBoost because it trains fast and it's efficient to serve in production.
I would choose XG Boost over deep learning when the problem is mainly based on some structure feature, when the data set is not, extremely large, and the iteration speed...
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「lean toward X, if Z changes switch to Y」vs 一长串 when… when… 不收口。
why: 说「I'd lean toward XGBoost, but if the data gets huge, switch to deep learning」——默认加翻转条件一次说清，别堆 when… when…。
why_en: Say "I'd lean toward XGBoost, but if the data gets huge or unstructured I'd switch to deep learning," instead of stacking when... when... clauses.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据本来就是图像、文本这类非结构化，那默认就该是深度学习，XGBoost 反而是被翻转的一方。
options_en: It depends on the data really — sometimes XGBoost is better and sometimes deep learning is better, it's kind of case by case.
For structured, smaller data I'd lean toward XGBoost for speed. But if the data gets huge or unstructured, I'd switch to deep learning.
I'd just go with XGBoost because it trains fast and it's efficient to serve in production.
I would choose XG Boost over deep learning when the problem is mainly based on some structure feature, when the data set is not, extremely large, and the iteration speed...
optionMeanings: 选项主张：只说看情况、case by case，不拍板。
选项主张：先定默认模型，数据变大再换。
选项主张：只夸它快，不给翻转条件。
选项主张：一长串 when… when… 不收口。
optionScenarioImpacts: 看情况等于没答，显得没主见。
默认选择加翻转条件，一次说清。
只讲优点，没说什么时候不该用它。
堆一串条件却不落地，听着卡。
optionMeanings_en: Only say it depends, case by case, no commit.
Fix a default model, switch when data grows.
Praise its speed, give no switch condition.
Stack a long run of when... when... clauses.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "It depends" answers nothing and reads as no opinion.
Default plus switch condition, said in one pass.
Upside only, never says when not to use it.
Stacked clauses that never land sound stuck.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: it depends.
Use when you state a default and its switch condition.
Only fits when this statement is true: upside only.
Only fits when this statement is true: clauses never land.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种基于梯度提升树的模型，擅长结构化表格数据；读作「X-G-Boost」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XGBoost is a gradient-boosted decision-tree model that's strong on structured, tabular data.

scenario: Majestic 面试讲前端为何慢。她绕成「in the short term we still have the latency because we recall the existing API twice... we call it once, then they change it, then we call it again」，一直重复没拍板。
scenario_en: In the Majestic interview she explains why the frontend is slow, looping on "we still have the latency because we recall the existing API twice... we call it once, then they change it, then we call it again" without committing.
q: 「把两次 API 调用合成一次以降延迟」，怎么用「I'd lean toward X because…」拍板？
q_en: How do you commit to "merge the two API calls into one" with "I'd lean toward X because..."?
options: In the short term we still have the latency because we recall the existing API twice, so when the user lands we call it once, then they change it, then we call it again...
The frontend felt a bit slow, so I looked into the API calls and tried to make the page load faster somehow.
I merged the two calls into one so the page just loads faster for the user, problem solved.
The page made two API calls, so I'd lean toward merging them into one — it saves a round trip and about a second, at the cost of a heavier backend call.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「I'd lean toward X because…」+ 代价 vs 「we call it once, then… then」重复不拍板。
why: 「lean toward merging them because it saves a round trip」把决定和收益说出，再补代价（后端更重）；别重复 call once、call again。
why_en: Say "I'd lean toward merging the two calls because it saves a round trip and a second," then add the cost — don't loop on "call it once, then call it again."
whenOtherWins: 如果那两次调用取的是两块彼此独立的数据，合并反而把后端拖慢，那分开两次调用更好。
options_en: In the short term we still have the latency because we recall the existing API twice, so when the user lands we call it once, then they change it, then we call it again...
The frontend felt a bit slow, so I looked into the API calls and tried to make the page load faster somehow.
I merged the two calls into one so the page just loads faster for the user, problem solved.
The page made two API calls, so I'd lean toward merging them into one — it saves a round trip and about a second, at the cost of a heavier backend call.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：反复描述两次调用却不下决定。
选项主张：泛泛说慢、试着弄快点。
选项主张：只说合并后更快，不提代价。
选项主张：拍板合并并讲清收益，再补代价。
optionScenarioImpacts: 重复描述没决定，面试官等不到结论。
含糊「弄快点」，听不出你做了什么。
只讲好处，漏掉后端更重的代价。
决定加收益一句清，还收了代价的尾。
optionMeanings_en: Repeat call once / call again, never commit.
Vaguely say slow and tried to speed it up.
Say merging is faster, no cost mentioned.
Commit to merging and state gain, then add cost.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Repeated description with no decision leaves them waiting.
"Made it faster" doesn't say what you actually did.
Upside only, drops the heavier backend cost.
Decision plus gain in one line, cost closed out.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: repeat with no decision.
Only fits when this statement is true: vague speed-up.
Only fits when this statement is true: faster, no cost.
Use when you commit to merging and name the cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次「请求发出去、响应回来」的完整往返；少一个 round trip 就省一段网络延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is one full request-out, response-back cycle; cutting one saves that slice of network latency.

scenario: Alterion 面试问前后端用 GraphQL 还是 REST。她说「GraphQL make the front end lighter... if we use RESTful API we need to validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with back end」，措辞乱、没拍板。
scenario_en: In the Alterion interview she's asked GraphQL or REST for frontend-backend. She says "GraphQL make the front end lighter... if we use RESTful API we need to validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with backend" — muddled, no commitment.
q: 该怎么点名 GraphQL vs REST 的取舍并拍板？
q_en: How do you name the GraphQL vs REST tradeoff and commit?
options: The tradeoff is GraphQL versus REST: GraphQL lets the frontend fetch exactly what it needs, but costs more server complexity. For this UI I'd lean GraphQL.
I'd use GraphQL because it makes the frontend lighter and you can fetch everything you need in a single query.
GraphQL make the front end lighter, so, if we use RESTful API then we need to validate the passing parameters, if the structure is, cracked with the backend, and do some conversion.
I'd pick whichever of GraphQL or REST fits the frontend better, it kind of depends on the case.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「GraphQL versus REST」+ 拍板 vs 「the structure is cracked」措辞乱、不落地。
why: 先点名「GraphQL versus REST」，说清 GraphQL 精确取数的好处和服务端更复杂的代价，再拍板。她的问题是措辞乱、never lands。
why_en: Name it — GraphQL versus REST — give GraphQL's precise-fetching upside and its server-complexity cost, then commit.
whenOtherWins: 如果接口简单、只有几个固定资源，REST 更省心；这时 GraphQL 的服务端复杂度就不值得。
options_en: The tradeoff is GraphQL versus REST: GraphQL lets the frontend fetch exactly what it needs, but costs more server complexity. For this UI I'd lean GraphQL.
I'd use GraphQL because it makes the frontend lighter and you can fetch everything you need in a single query.
GraphQL make the front end lighter, so, if we use RESTful API then we need to validate the passing parameters, if the structure is, cracked with the backend, and do some conversion.
I'd pick whichever of GraphQL or REST fits the frontend better, it kind of depends on the case.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：点名两者取舍，讲清代价后拍板。
选项主张：只夸 GraphQL 轻、一次取全，不提代价。
选项主张：措辞乱掉，判断没落地。
选项主张：泛泛说看情况选更合适的。
optionScenarioImpacts: 点名加拍板，好处代价都交代了。
只讲好处，漏掉服务端更复杂的代价。
措辞一乱，面试官抓不到你的判断。
看情况等于没选，收不了尾。
optionMeanings_en: GraphQL versus REST, name the cost, then commit.
Praise GraphQL's fetching, mention no cost.
"Cracked with backend" is muddled and never lands.
Vaguely pick whichever fits better.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Names it and commits, upside and cost both covered.
Upside only, drops the server-complexity cost.
Muddled wording hides your actual judgment.
"It depends" makes no choice and trails off.
optionDirectness_en: Use when you name the axis, the cost, then commit.
Only fits when this statement is true: upside only.
Only fits when this statement is true: muddled wording.
Only fits when this statement is true: no choice made.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言，前端用一次请求精确取到需要的字段；代价是服务端要维护 schema、解析更复杂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the frontend fetch exactly the fields it needs in one request, at the cost of more server-side complexity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按资源划分固定端点的接口风格；简单直接，但前端常要多次调用或拿到多余字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST exposes fixed per-resource endpoints — simple, but the frontend often makes several calls or gets extra fields it doesn't need.

scenario: Gamma 面试问 campaign settings（类型、ROI 目标、预算、日期、product 级信息）怎么存。她容易列一堆方案却不拍板，卡在「keeping it simple and flexible」那种打转里。
scenario_en: In the Gamma interview she's asked how to store campaign settings (type, ROI goal, budget, dates, product-level info). She tends to list options without committing, drifting into that "simple and flexible" loop.
q: 面对「关系型还是文档型存储」，怎么避免只罗列、直接拍板说出口？
q_en: For "relational vs document store," how do you avoid just listing and commit out loud?
options: We could use a relational model, or maybe a NoSQL one, honestly there are pros and cons on both sides, so it really depends on a lot of different factors here, I think...
I'd use a relational database because everything is structured and relational, so it just fits.
These settings are structured and queried together, so I'd lean toward a relational store. If the schema starts varying per campaign, I'd switch to a document store.
There are various storage options with different tradeoffs that would need to be evaluated for this use case.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「I'd lean toward X, if Z changes switch to Y」拍板 vs 列方案却 depends on factors 不选。
why: 先拍板选关系型（因为字段结构化、要一起查），再给翻转条件（schema 按 campaign 变就换文档型）。她的毛病是罗列 pros and cons、never lands。
why_en: Commit to relational because the fields are structured and queried together, then give the switch condition — go document store if the schema starts varying per campaign.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个 campaign 的字段差别很大、schema 频繁变动，那文档型更合适，关系型的固定表结构反而拖累。
options_en: We could use a relational model, or maybe a NoSQL one, honestly there are pros and cons on both sides, so it really depends on a lot of different factors here, I think...
I'd use a relational database because everything is structured and relational, so it just fits.
These settings are structured and queried together, so I'd lean toward a relational store. If the schema starts varying per campaign, I'd switch to a document store.
There are various storage options with different tradeoffs that would need to be evaluated for this use case.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：列一堆利弊、说看情况却不选。
选项主张：拍了板但没给翻转条件。
选项主张：拍板选关系型，schema 变就换文档型。
选项主张：泛泛说有多种方案要评估。
optionScenarioImpacts: 罗列不选，显得你没能力拍板。
选了但没说何时会反转，缺一层。
拍板加翻转条件，判断完整。
空话一句，等于没碰这个决定。
optionMeanings_en: List pros and cons, "depends," never choose.
Commits but gives no switch condition.
Commit to relational, switch to document if schema varies.
Vaguely say several options need evaluating.

Chose it but never says when it flips — a layer missing.
Commitment plus switch condition, complete judgment.
Empty line that never touches the decision.

Use when you commit and give the switch condition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把每条记录存成自带结构 JSON 文档的 NoSQL 数据库，schema 可逐条不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document store is a NoSQL database that keeps each record as a self-describing JSON document, so the schema can differ row to row.
